decision: The scanner panel is the primary surface; the list follows it
why: Eyes stay on the product and barcode, so the next item, prompt and progress ring live where the camera is.
alternative: A checklist with a small scan button per row.
value: One motion per item: point, beep, next.

decision: Each scan is an idempotent command keyed by order, SKU and unit
why: Scanners double-fire and offline queues replay; a duplicate must not over-pick.
alternative: Increment a counter on every scan event.
value: Offline replays and double beeps can't corrupt the pick list.

decision: 'Can't find it?' writes a stock correction, not just a note
why: A missing item means the availability data was wrong; fixing it here protects the next customer.
alternative: Free-text comment sent to a manager.
value: Store-level stock accuracy improves as a side effect of normal work.

decision: Substitutes are ranked by fit and stock, then offered to the customer to accept
why: Similarity is useful for ranking, but the customer decides whether a replacement is acceptable.
value: Fewer cancelled orders without surprising anyone at pickup.

decision: Progress is a filling ring with a count, not a percentage bar
why: Orders are 1–4 items; '2/3' is what a picker says out loud.
alternative: A thin percentage bar at the top.
value: State is readable at arm's length on a tablet.
